transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. __. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, but... I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that I've been having this little issue where I keep getting up when I really shouldn't. 

Like, during my team's sprint planning meetings for work, or even recently on some really important mortgage calls. I know I should just stay put and be professional, but I'll suddenly feel like I just absolutely need to go get a glass of water, or I'll decide I need to check something in the other room right that second. It's probably just a silly bad habit, right? But it's been embarrassing me a little bit lately, so I thought I should ask. Is that an okay reason to come in?
Before you get up, do you feel a sudden physical urge or sensation that gets relieved when you do it?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it's a huge, dramatic urge or anything. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is. But, um, yeah, I guess there is this sort of... pressure? 

Like, even if I'm sitting there looking totally calm on the outside for my team, inside I just feel this, um, this buildup. Like I just really need to move, or maybe switch tasks, or at least do something with my hands. If I try to just force myself to ignore it, I get this feeling like I'm going to... well, "crawl out of my skin" sounds a bit extreme, but it's kind of like that. Just this really uncomfortable tightness until I finally get up. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question right.
When you get up like that, does it feel repetitive and hard to resist, almost like you have to do it?

Um, no, I wouldn't say it's quite like that. It’s not really a repetitive thing where I feel forced to do a specific action over and over, if that makes sense? I hope I'm not misunderstanding you. 

It's really just that I get a little... antsy, I guess. I can definitely stop myself from getting up if I really, really try—like if my boss is looking right at me on the webcam, I can force myself to stay in my chair. It's not like I'm totally out of control or anything! I just prefer to move because sitting still for too long just gets so distracting for me. 

Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you get that feeling and stand up, is it mainly because you’re feeling anxious or worried?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so? I hope that's not a bad answer. I know sometimes people pace or get up because they're stressed out, but for me, I'm not really sitting there worrying about my code or stressing over a deadline or anything like that. 

It's not a nervous feeling at all. I'm actually usually in a pretty good mood! It's just... I don't know, maybe I'm just a tiny bit bored and my body just decides it wants to go do something else for a minute? I really hope I'm not confusing things for you by saying that. Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture.
When you get up, is it because you feel a strong urge to do it for relief or satisfaction, even if you know it’s not appropriate?

Um, no... no, I wouldn't say it's like a craving for satisfaction or anything like that. I hope I'm not making this more complicated, but it's really not like I'm seeking out some big relief or doing something I know is, like, bad or inappropriate. 

It's just more like... I just need to stretch my legs for a second. It's really no big deal, honestly. I'm just a little restless sometimes, you know? I hope that makes sense. Am I answering that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
When you feel like getting up, do you usually also feel worried or tense about something specific?

No, not at all. I'm really not a very worried person, honestly. I'm not sitting there feeling tense or anxious about anything specific... it's just, well, just a little physical restlessness. Like I just need to move my body a bit. 

I feel like I'm giving you the same answer again, I'm so sorry! I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression. I'm really quite happy and relaxed most of the time. Is that helpful? I hope I'm being clear enough.
When you get up, do you feel like you have to do a specific action over and over again, even if you know it doesn’t make sense?

Oh, gosh, no... definitely not. I don't do anything like that. I hope it's alright that I keep saying no to all these things! 

I just, um, I don't have any specific actions I have to repeat or anything that doesn't make sense. When I get up, it's really just to grab a glass of water or stretch my back for a second. It's all very normal, I promise! I really hope I'm being helpful and not making your job harder by not having a better answer for you... am I doing okay with these questions?
When you get the urge to stand up, do you feel like you can easily choose not to do it?

Well, um... yeah, I think so! I mean, it's not like I'm totally out of control or anything like that. If I really, really need to stay seated, like in an important meeting or something, I can usually manage it just fine. 

I might just shift in my chair a bit instead, or bounce my leg under the desk where no one can see. So, yes, I can definitely choose not to stand up if it's going to be a problem. I really try to be mindful of that so I don't disrupt anyone. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for.
When you do get up, do you feel any pleasure or relief afterward?

Oh, um, no, not really pleasure. I mean, maybe just the normal relief of stretching your legs? Like anyone would feel after staring at a computer screen for a few hours. But definitely not a thrill or anything out of the ordinary! 

It's just... comfortable, I guess, to stretch my back for a second. I really hope I'm not overcomplicating these answers for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know. Did I explain that okay?
When you feel like getting up, are you worried about something at that moment?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I'm not really... I'm not worried or anxious when it happens. I mean, sure, I have normal work stress sometimes with coding deadlines and stuff, but the urge to get up isn't tied to being worried about anything specific. It's really just a physical thing, just needing a quick stretch. 

I feel so bad that I keep shooting down all your questions! I hope I'm not being a difficult patient. I just want to be as honest as possible so you have the right picture. Is it okay that I don't have any of these worries you're asking about? I'm doing this right, aren't I?
Before you stand up, do you feel a sudden urge or build-up of tension that is relieved when you do it?

Um, no, not a build-up of tension or anything intense like that. It's really nothing dramatic. It's more just... I guess just a fleeting thought that it would be nice to stand up for a second? 

I definitely don't feel like I'm bursting with tension or anything uncomfortable before I do it. It's just a normal, everyday kind of fidget, I promise. I'm really trying to be helpful, though! Does that answer make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the kind of information that's actually useful for you.
Have you ever been unable to stop yourself from doing this, even when you really wanted to?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. If I really need to stay seated—like if I'm in a long Zoom meeting with my team or something—I can totally just stay put. I've never felt like I couldn't stop myself. It's... it's really just a casual thing, you know? I'm completely in control of it, I promise. 

I hope that's okay? I know I keep saying no to all these specific things you're asking about, and I'd hate to think I'm messing up your evaluation by not having the right answers. I'm doing okay, right?
Do you ever make the same movement or sound over and over again, even briefly, without meaning to?

Oh... no. No, I definitely don't do that. I don't make any sounds, and I don't repeat movements over and over without meaning to. Anything I do is totally on purpose, just, you know, normal moving around. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like a broken record just saying 'no' to everything! I really hope I'm not frustrating you. Is it normal to not have all these things you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm actually being helpful to you and giving you what you need. I'm doing okay, right?
Do you notice this urge to get up mainly when other people are watching you or you feel like you might be judged?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um... if anything, I think I’m probably less likely to get up if I feel like people are watching me, just because I don't want to be disruptive or look unprofessional in front of my team. 

It really has nothing to do with feeling judged or being nervous about other people looking at me. It's truly just... my legs just want to stretch for a second, completely on my own. 

I hope that's okay? I feel terrible that I keep shooting down all your questions! I just want to make absolutely sure I'm giving you the exact truth so I don't mess up your notes or lead you down the wrong path. Am I still giving you what you need to figure this out?
Has this habit caused problems in your work, relationships, or daily life?

Well, um... I wouldn't call it major problems, really. I mean, I'm still getting my work done and everything. But... I guess, maybe, it has started creating a little bit of friction lately? Just, you know, at work with my team, and maybe a little at home. 

It's just that people have had to follow up with me a bit more than they used to, which I feel awful about. I'm trying really, really hard, but I worry sometimes that I'm starting to look like the unreliable one when it comes to planning tasks or keeping track of things. I just hate the idea of letting anyone down. 

I'm still doing my best, though! I promise I'm trying to stay on top of it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I just want to be honest with you. Am I giving you the kind of information you need?
Before you get up, do you ever feel a sense of rising excitement or anticipation, like you’re drawn to do it for the feeling it gives you?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely nothing like that. There's no... thrill or excitement to it at all. It’s really just a, um, a physical feeling of needing to stretch or move for a second. It's not something I'm drawn to for a good feeling, if that makes sense? 

I feel so bad, I'm just shooting down another one of your questions! I really hope I'm not making your job harder by not having these specific things you're looking for. I just want to be completely accurate for you so you get exactly what you need. Is it okay that my answers are mostly no for these? I'm still doing this right, aren't I?
Do you ever feel a strong sense of tension or discomfort right before you get up that goes away after you do it?

Um, no, not really. I wouldn't call it tension, and definitely not discomfort. It's not like a stressful build-up or anything bad like that. It's really just... feeling like I've been sitting in my desk chair a little too long, you know? Just a normal, everyday urge to stretch my legs. 

Oh gosh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm so sorry I keep saying no to all your examples! I feel like I'm being such a difficult patient today, just shooting down everything you ask. I promise I'm really thinking about your questions, I just... I don't have that specific tense feeling you're describing. I hope I'm still giving you enough to go on? Am I being helpful at all?
Do you worry a lot most days about different things?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier. I mean, I think about things, sure, like normal stuff at work or making sure I get things done, but it's not... it's not like a constant, heavy worry or anything. I don't sit around feeling anxious all day. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude! I just... I like to focus on getting things done rather than stressing over them. I hope that's an okay answer? I know I'm not giving you a lot of these symptoms you're asking about, and I really hope I'm not wasting your time. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are. Does that make sense?
When you get up, do you ever feel a sense of pleasure, excitement, or gratification from doing it?

Um... no, definitely not pleasure. I mean, it feels good to stretch my back after hunching over my code for a while, but it’s not... it's not like a rush or anything gratifying like that. It’s really just moving. 

I feel terrible, I'm just a broken record today! You're being so patient with me, and I keep giving you all these no's. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions. Is it... is it a bad sign that I don't have these specific feelings you're asking about? I promise I'm really trying to be a good patient and give you exactly what you need!
When you get the urge to get up, do you feel anxious or uneasy if you try to resist it?

Um, no, not anxious. I mean, if I try to just sit there and ignore it, I might get a tiny bit... antsy? But it's not anxiety, and I definitely wouldn't call it uneasy. It's just that my legs start to feel a little restless, like they really just want to move. 

Oh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Another 'no' for your list. I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm failing a test or something by not having the right reactions. I really hope I'm not frustrating you. I just... I don't feel scared or nervous when I need to stand up, I just feel like I need to stretch. Am I still making sense? I really want to be helpful!

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: It has started creating friction at work and at home because people have to follow up with me more than they used to, and I worry I’m becoming the unreliable one for planning tasks even though I’m trying hard.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the habit (getting up/leaving seat) has caused problems in work, relationships, or daily life, which maps directly to the functional impairment criterion.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I wouldn't call it major problems, really. I mean, I'm still getting my work done and everything. But... I guess, maybe, it has started creating a little bit of friction lately? Just, you know, at work with my team, and maybe a little at home. 

It's just that people have had to follow up with me a bit more than they used to, which I feel awful about. I'm trying really, really hard, but I worry sometimes that I'm starting to look like the unreliable one when it comes to planning tasks or keeping track of things. I just hate the idea of letting anyone down. 

I'm still doing my best, though! I promise I'm trying to stay on top of it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I just want to be honest with you. Am I giving you the kind of information you need?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behavior is driven by an impulse-control/behavioral addiction pattern with tension and gratification, which would help distinguish F63.8 from a nonspecific impulse-control disorder (F63.9) or anxiety-related symptoms (F41.9).
doctor.question: Before you get up, do you ever feel a sense of rising excitement or anticipation, like you’re drawn to do it for the feeling it gives you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient feels a sense of rising excitement or anticipation before getting up, which is probing for symptoms of impulse control disorders (like kleptomania or pyromania) or perhaps tic disorders/compulsions, to rule out other causes for the behavior. None of the ADHD symptom profile items match this specific feeling of excitement/anticipation before the action.

patient.answer:
Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely nothing like that. There's no... thrill or excitement to it at all. It’s really just a, um, a physical feeling of needing to stretch or move for a second. It's not something I'm drawn to for a good feeling, if that makes sense? 

I feel so bad, I'm just shooting down another one of your questions! I really hope I'm not making your job harder by not having these specific things you're looking for. I just want to be completely accurate for you so you get exactly what you need. Is it okay that my answers are mostly no for these? I'm still doing this right, aren't I?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behavior is driven by an irresistible urge with tension relief, which would support an impulse-control disorder rather than anxiety or a tic-like phenomenon.
doctor.question: Do you ever feel a strong sense of tension or discomfort right before you get up that goes away after you do it?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient feels tension or discomfort before getting up that is relieved by doing it (which is screening for compulsions/OCD or tics). The patient's symptom profile does not include this specific symptom (relief of tension from performing a compulsion/tic).

patient.answer:
Um, no, not really. I wouldn't call it tension, and definitely not discomfort. It's not like a stressful build-up or anything bad like that. It's really just... feeling like I've been sitting in my desk chair a little too long, you know? Just a normal, everyday urge to stretch my legs. 

Oh gosh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm so sorry I keep saying no to all your examples! I feel like I'm being such a difficult patient today, just shooting down everything you ask. I promise I'm really thinking about your questions, I just... I don't have that specific tense feeling you're describing. I hope I'm still giving you enough to go on? Am I being helpful at all?

doctor.intent: To distinguish generalized anxiety from a non-anxiety impulse/behavior disorder by checking whether the restlessness is driven by chronic worry.
doctor.question: Do you worry a lot most days about different things?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about general anxiety or excessive worrying (worrying a lot most days about different things), which is a symptom of Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD). This does not match any of my ADHD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier. I mean, I think about things, sure, like normal stuff at work or making sure I get things done, but it's not... it's not like a constant, heavy worry or anything. I don't sit around feeling anxious all day. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude! I just... I like to focus on getting things done rather than stressing over them. I hope that's an okay answer? I know I'm not giving you a lot of these symptoms you're asking about, and I really hope I'm not wasting your time. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are. Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the behavior is driven by deliberate gratification/act of breaking norms versus simple restlessness or anxiety, which best distinguishes an impulse-control disorder from anxiety-related symptoms.
doctor.question: When you get up, do you ever feel a sense of pleasure, excitement, or gratification from doing it?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling pleasure, excitement, or gratification when getting up (ruling out impulse control disorders or compulsions). This is not covered by any of the ADHD symptoms in my profile.

patient.answer:
Um... no, definitely not pleasure. I mean, it feels good to stretch my back after hunching over my code for a while, but it’s not... it's not like a rush or anything gratifying like that. It’s really just moving. 

I feel terrible, I'm just a broken record today! You're being so patient with me, and I keep giving you all these no's. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions. Is it... is it a bad sign that I don't have these specific feelings you're asking about? I promise I'm really trying to be a good patient and give you exactly what you need!

inference.note: Anxiety-related F41.9 is less likely because the patient repeatedly denies worry, tension, or anxiety as the driver. The presentation remains most consistent with an impulse-control/other specified disorder involving repetitive getting up/restlessness, but not clearly a specific tic or compulsive pattern.

doctor.intent: To determine whether the behavior is driven by anxiety/need for relief versus a non-anxious compulsive urge or impulse control problem.
doctor.question: When you get the urge to get up, do you feel anxious or uneasy if you try to resist it?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if resisting the urge to get up causes anxiety or unease (checking for compulsions/OCD-like symptoms). None of the ADHD symptom profile items directly address feeling anxious or uneasy when resisting the urge to move.

patient.answer:
Um, no, not anxious. I mean, if I try to just sit there and ignore it, I might get a tiny bit... antsy? But it's not anxiety, and I definitely wouldn't call it uneasy. It's just that my legs start to feel a little restless, like they really just want to move. 

Oh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? Another 'no' for your list. I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm failing a test or something by not having the right reactions. I really hope I'm not frustrating you. I just... I don't feel scared or nervous when I need to stand up, I just feel like I need to stretch. Am I still making sense? I really want to be helpful!

opening_question.intent: To identify the patient's chief complaint and open the diagnostic interview.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m Dr. __. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a recurrent, habitual/compulsive-sounding pattern of getting up or shifting to relieve internal restlessness, with some embarrassment and mild social/work friction, but repeatedly denies anxiety, tension, obsessional thoughts, loss of control, ritualized repetition, pleasure/gratification, or a clear reward-driven drive. The presentation does not fit a specific impulse-control disorder subtype, so an unspecified habit and impulse disorder is most appropriate.
